input.title: Lazy sync would create one forced channel per opened document, because the forward-only cursor forbids widening a live channel's filter

input.description: Each lazily opened document gets a channel scoped by filter.documentId that backfills from ordinal 0; channels dedup by documentId and stay synced for the session. N open documents means N channels.

This is the mechanism the proposal rests on; the parent note is what its status and problem statement are

input.content:
The unit of laziness in ADR 0001 is a **document channel**, created on demand — and the ADR is explicit that these channels are "forced, not chosen": the forward-only, collection-wide cursor forbids mutating the drive channel's filter to add a document (`touchChannel` discards changed filters), so the only way to backfill one document is a fresh channel scoped by `filter.documentId`, which auto-backfills that document's full history from ordinal 0. Channels dedup by `documentId` and stay synced for the session.

The API surface stays small: `addRemoteDrive(url, { preloadDocuments })` defaults to today's eager behaviour, and `false` registers only a drive-only channel; new `addRemoteDocument` / `removeRemoteDocument` verbs open and release document channels. Provisioning is deliberately an **internal strategy** rather than more booleans, so future policies do not each add a flag, and the eager default stays byte-identical to today.

The cost is stated as a risk, not hidden: **N open documents = N logical channels.** Coalesced batch polling with chunking collapses poll cost to `ceil(N / chunk)` requests per endpoint per tick, so it is not a scaling ceiling — but that transport work is a **prerequisite** for opening lazy drives at scale, and the ADR records only medium confidence in the batch-poll scaling claim, unverified at thousands of open documents.

Two more consequences: `preloadDocuments:false` **breaks whole-drive-assuming consumers** — code that iterates `state.global.nodes` and calls `useDocuments(childIds)` or `find({parentId})` hits misses or suspends, and `useDocuments` returns a *silent partial list*, so every such caller must be audited before flipping the flag. And the write path is unchanged: a lazily-synced document pushes on its own channel.
